title: Scramble String
description:
# Scramble String

We can scramble a string s to get a string t using the following algorithm:

1.  If the length of the string is 1, stop.
2.  If the length of the string is > 1, do the following:
    *   Split the string into two non-empty substrings at a random index, i.e., if the string is `s`, divide it to `x` and `y` where `s = x + y`.
    *   Randomly decide to swap the two substrings or to keep them in the same order. i.e., after this step, `s` may become `s = x + y` or `s = y + x`.
    *   Apply step 1 recursively on each of the two substrings `x` and `y`.

Given two strings `s1` and `s2` of **the same length**, return `true` if `s2` is a scrambled string of `s1`, otherwise, return `false`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s1 = "great", s2 = "rgeat"
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** One possible scenario applied on s1 is:
"great" --> "gr/eat" // divide at random index.
"gr/eat" --> "gr/eat" // random decision is not to swap the two substrings and keep them in order.
"gr/eat" --> "g/r / e/at" // apply the same algorithm recursively on both substrings. divide at random index each of them.
"g/r / e/at" --> "r/g / e/at" // random decision was to swap the first substring and to keep the second substring in the same order.
"r/g / e/at" --> "r/g / e/ a/t" // again apply the algorithm recursively, divide "at" to "a/t".
"r/g / e/ a/t" --> "r/g / e/ a/t" // random decision is to keep both substrings in the same order.
The algorithm stops now and the result string is "rgeat" which is s2.
As there is one possible scenario that led s1 to be scrambled to s2, we return true.

## Example 2:

**Input:** s1 = "abcde", s2 = "caebd"
**Output:** false

## Example 3:

**Input:** s1 = "a", s2 = "a"
**Output:** true

## Constraints:

*   `s1.length == s2.length`
*   `1 <= s1.length <= 30`
*   `s1` and `s2` consist of lowercase English letters.

solutions.name: 3D Dynamic Programming
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a bottom-up interval DP where `dp[len][i][j]` means `s1.substring(i, i + len)` can scramble into `s2.substring(j, j + len)`. Initialize length-1 states by character equality, then increase the interval length.

## Key Insight

For a fixed split length `k`, either the left part maps to the left part and the right part maps to the right part, or the two children are swapped. Those two cases exactly match the recursive scramble definition.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^4)
- Space Complexity: O(n^3)

solutions.name: Recursive with Memoization
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use top-down recursion on the two current substrings and memoize each `(leftSubstring, rightSubstring)` pair in a hash map. Before trying split points, compare character frequencies to reject impossible pairs.

## Key Insight

Scramble equivalence has overlapping subproblems: the same pair of substrings can be reached through different split orders. Memoization keeps the recursion from expanding the same interval pair repeatedly.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^4)
- Space Complexity: O(n^3)

solutions.name: Index DFS With Prefix Counts
solutions.description:
## Approach

Memoize states by `(i, j, len)` instead of allocating substring objects. Prefix character counts check whether the two intervals contain the same multiset of letters before the DFS tries split points.

## Key Insight

The recursive state is fully determined by two starting indices and one length. Using prefix counts gives the same pruning as substring frequency checks while staying close to interval DP.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^4)
- Space Complexity: O(n^3)
solutions.code: class Solution { private String a, b; private Boolean[][][] memo; private int[][] prefA, prefB; public boolean isScramble(String s1, String s2) { int n = s1.length(); a = s1; b = s2; memo = new Boolean[n][n][n + 1]; prefA = buildPrefix(a); prefB = buildPrefix(b); return dfs(0, 0, n); } private boolean dfs(int i, int j, int len) { if (a.regionMatches(i, b, j, len)) return true; if (memo[i][j][len] != null) return memo[i][j][len]; if (!sameCounts(i, j, len)) return memo[i][j][len] = false; for (int split = 1; split < len; split++) { if (dfs(i, j, split) && dfs(i + split, j + split, len - split)) return memo[i][j][len] = true; if (dfs(i, j + len - split, split) && dfs(i + split, j, len - split)) return memo[i][j][len] = true; } return memo[i][j][len] = false; } private int[][] buildPrefix(String s) { int[][] pref = new int[s.length() + 1][26]; for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) { System.arraycopy(pref[i], 0, pref[i + 1], 0, 26); pref[i + 1][s.charAt(i) - 'a']++; } return pref; } private boolean sameCounts(int i, int j, int len) { for (int c = 0; c < 26; c++) { int ca = prefA[i + len][c] - prefA[i][c]; int cb = prefB[j + len][c] - prefB[j][c]; if (ca != cb) return false; } return true; } }

solutions.name: Prefix-Pruned Bottom-Up DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build prefix letter counts for both strings, then run the same length-first interval DP. For each `(len, i, j)` state, skip all split checks if the two intervals do not have identical character counts.

## Key Insight

Character-count equality is necessary for scramble equivalence. Applying that filter inside bottom-up DP keeps the deterministic table order while avoiding split work on impossible interval pairs.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^4)
- Space Complexity: O(n^3)
solutions.code: class Solution { public boolean isScramble(String s1, String s2) { int n = s1.length(); int[][] prefA = buildPrefix(s1); int[][] prefB = buildPrefix(s2); boolean[][][] dp = new boolean[n + 1][n][n]; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) { dp[1][i][j] = s1.charAt(i) == s2.charAt(j); } } for (int len = 2; len <= n; len++) { for (int i = 0; i <= n - len; i++) { for (int j = 0; j <= n - len; j++) { if (!sameCounts(prefA, prefB, i, j, len)) continue; for (int split = 1; split < len; split++) { if ((dp[split][i][j] && dp[len - split][i + split][j + split]) || (dp[split][i][j + len - split] && dp[len - split][i + split][j])) { dp[len][i][j] = true; break; } } } } } return dp[n][0][0]; } private int[][] buildPrefix(String s) { int[][] pref = new int[s.length() + 1][26]; for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) { System.arraycopy(pref[i], 0, pref[i + 1], 0, 26); pref[i + 1][s.charAt(i) - 'a']++; } return pref; } private boolean sameCounts(int[][] prefA, int[][] prefB, int i, int j, int len) { for (int c = 0; c < 26; c++) { int left = prefA[i + len][c] - prefA[i][c]; int right = prefB[j + len][c] - prefB[j][c]; if (left != right) return false; } return true; } }
